This packet also includes a vote to compensate land owners for each individual taking. We are requesting that the City Council hold a public hearing and consider voting on this matter at their September 16, 2026 meeting. The City was awarded an FY2025 HousingWorks grant to address public safety and accessibility concerns at the Parsons Street and Ferry Street intersection. This grant funds work to improve vehicle sightlines and to increase pedestrian safety and connectivity by creating a new sidewalk on the south side of Ferry Street. In order to accomplish these improvements, an existing retaining wall will be relocated several feet back from the roadway. Additionally, two crosswalks with rapid-flashing beacons will be installed on Ferry Street. These improvements require the City to acquire permanent and temporary construction easements on a total of eight properties. The City has communicated with all affected property owners since April 2026 and recently acquired appraisals for the permanent and temporary easements. Owners of two properties donated their easements to the City and Just Compensation Reports for the remaining properties were sent to owners in July 2026, along with notification of the City Council public hearing. The project design plans and easement plans are posted on the Planning Department website (https://www.easthamptonma.gov/978/Ferry-Street-HousingWorks-Infrastructure). The City’s team includes the City Planner, City Engineer and DPW Director, the design consultant (VHB), the City’s appraiser (Crowley and Associates), and the City Solicitor. The requested action from City Council includes voting on the Order of Taking to take the easements and an appropriation of $50,810 to pay property owners from the Parsons & Ferry Intersection Capital Project account. The following information is included in this packet: 1. Resolution 2. Order of Taking a. Exhibit A - Order of Taking with Exhibits b. Exhibit B - Chart of Payments c. Exhibit C - Donations 3. KOCH CITY OF QUINCY IN COUNCIL ORDER NO. 2026-122 ORDERED: September 22 2026 WHEREAS, the City of Quincy is constructing two new parking garages in the downtown as part of its urban renewal efforts; one garage located at 86 Parkingway a/k/a 25-55 General McConville Way, and the second located at 119 Parkingway a/k/a 101 General McConville Way, each in the City of Quincy; and WHEREAS, the City of Quincy seeks to reduce the financial burden on the tax payers of Quincy related to the operating costs of all city-owned buildings; seeks to reduce its carbon footprint from municipal operations; and seeks to otherwise promote clean energy goals; and WHEREAS, the City of Quincy is a member of PowerOptions, Inc., a non-profit entity that, in association with the MassCEC which is the Commonwealth of Massachusetts’ economic development agency for accelerating clean energy, competitively procured renewable energy development services; and WHEREAS, as a result of that competitive process and pursuant to Massachusetts General Law Chapter 164 Section 137, PowerOptions selected Solect Energy Development, LLC, to provide solar energy development and other services; and WHEREAS, Solect Energy and PowerOptions have entered into an agreement governing the terms and conditions of Solect’s participation in the PowerOptions Solar Programs; and WHEREAS, the City of Quincy Department of Public Buildings has been engaged with and working in conjunction with Solect Energy for the design, installation and operation of a solar photovoltaic system to be installed by Solect Energy on structural canopies located above the top-level parking deck of each of these new parking garages; and WHEREAS, pursuant to Massachusetts General Law Chapter 164 Section 137, after having complied with the provisions of said Chapter 164 Section 137, the City of Quincy is exempt from further procurement provisions of any other Massachusetts law relative to the procurement of these solar energy development services and/or the solicitation of bids for the disposition of the City’s real estate interest in these parking garages for the development of these solar energy generation facilities; and ORDER NO. 2026 – 122 Page 2 of 2 WHEREAS, Solect Energy and the Department of Public Buildings acknowledge and agree that mandate of prevailing wages pursuant to Massachusetts General Law chapter 149 is in force and applicable for the installation of these solar electric energy generation facilities. WHEREAS, the installation and operation of the solar photovoltaic system at each of these new parking garages requires a disposition of a real estate interest of the City by the City per the terms of Massachusetts General Law Chapter 30B; NOW THEREFORE at the request of, and upon the recommendation of, the Commissioner of the Department of Public Buildings, the City Council does Order as follows: That pursuant to Massachusetts General Law Chapter 30B, the real property interest of the City of Quincy above the top level parking decks of each of these two new parking garages and other defined space within each said garage for associated equipment and interconnections are hereby declared to be available for disposition solely for the purpose of the installation, maintenance, renewal, replacement, interconnection, and operation of a solar photovoltaic system and the utilities and equipment related thereto; and Further, that the Mayor is hereby authorized to enter into and execute Lease and Easement agreements with Solect Energy Development, LLC, related to the above described real estate interests for the purpose of the development and operation as stated of solar electric energy generation, upon the terms and conditions that the Mayor deems to be in the best interest of the City; Further, that the Mayor is hereby authorized to enter into and execute a Power Purchase Agreement with Solect Energy Development, LLC, its successors and assigns, for each of these two parking garages, for a term not to exceed twenty-five years, for the purpose of the development and operation as stated of solar electric energy generation, upon the terms and conditions that the Mayor deems to be in the best interest of the City;
